texts.preamble: Shoukath Pasha vs Shri K.Hariprasad Rao on 1 April, 2019 In The Court Of Iii Addl.Judge And Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Court Of Small Causes Bengaluru (Scch-18) Dated: This the 1st day of April 2019 Present: Sri.Mahantesh S.Dargad B.Sc., LL.B.,(Spl) Iii Addl. Judge & Member, Mact Court Of Small Causes, Bengaluru. M.V.C.No.5850/2017 Petitioner Shoukath Pasha, Son of Chand Pasha, Aged about 33 years, Residing at Kappalamadugu Village & Post, Mulabagal Taluk, Kolar District. (By Pleader Shri N.Giri Babu) V/s. Respondents 1.Shri K.Hariprasad Rao, Son of K.Kataiah, Major, Residing at No.501, Viswa Residency, Ccs Nagar, Dargamitta, Nellore, Andhra Pradesh-524 004. (By Pleader Shri C.R.Deva Reddy) 2 Scch-18 Mvc 5850/2017 2.The Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Company Limited, Golden Heights, 4th floor, No.1/2, 59th C cross, 4th 'M' Block, Rajajinagar, Bengaluru-560 010. (By Pleader Shri S.Maheshwara) J U D G M E N T
texts.facts: The petitioner has filed this claim petition U/S.166 of M.V. Act against the respondents claiming compensation amount of Rs.35,00,000/- on account of injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident. 2. The brief facts of the petition are as under: On 30.8.2015 at about 3.15 p.m. the petitioner was going towards Mulabagal from his village Kappalamadugu by riding his motor cycle bearing No.KA-51-L-4153 slowly, cautiously by observing all the traffic rules and regulations, when he reached near Narasimhatheertha cross, on four lane highway of Bengaluru- Chennai NH-75 road, at that time one Verna car bearing No.AP-26- AM-6556 driven by its driver with high speed in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger human life and safety of others and dashed against the motor cycle. Due to the impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries. Immediately he was shifted to R.L.Jalappa Hospital, Kolar, wherein he was treated as an inpatient. 3. Further the contention of the petitioner is that, prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy, aged about 33 years, Heavy Transport Vehicle driver and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month. The accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car bearing No.AP-26-AM-6556. Therefore, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation. Contending the above facts, he prays to grant for compensation with interest and cost. 4. In response to the petition notice, the respondents have appeared before the court and inspite of sufficient opportunities given to the respondent No.1 has not filed his written statement, so the written statement of the respondent No.1 is taken as not filed. The respondent No.2 has appeared before the court and filed its written statement. 5. The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.2 are as under: The respondent No.2 has contended in its written statement that the petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts. Further this respondent has admitted about the issuance of the policy in respect of vehicle bearing No. AP-26-AM- 6556 and its validity. Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111582972/ 2 6. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues were framed: 1. 7. In order to prove the case, the petitioner himself has examined as PW1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P10 and doctor is examined as PW2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P11 to Ex.P15. 8. To disprove the case of the petitioner and to prove the defence, the respondent No.2 has examined Manager, Jalappa hospital, Kolar and got marked the documents at Ex.R1 to Ex.R3 9.
texts.arguments: Further contended that neither the owner of the vehicle nor the jurisdictional police have complied the mandatory provisions of S. 134 and S. 158(6) of the M.V. Act in furnishing the better particulars. Further contended that the petitioner was not wearing helmet as on the date of accident. Further contended that the petitioner was solely responsible for the cause of accident. Further contended that the driver of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving licence to drive the same. Further contended that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the petitioner. Further denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner as alleged in the claim petition. Contending the above facts, he prays to dismiss the claim petition as against this respondent with cost. Further he argued that, to prove the disablement, the petitioner has examined Dr.Nagakumar as PW2, who has assessed 58.4% of whole body disability. Further he argued that the petitioner has proved his case as contended in the petition by producing oral and documentary evidence. Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition. 12. Per contra, the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 has denied the accident in toto, hence, prays to dismiss the petition as against the respondent No.2. 17. In addenda of this, in a claim for compensation U/S.166 of MV Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (Civil) 319 (Kusum and others Vs. Satbir and others). 24. The contention of the petitioner is that, he has spent huge amount towards medical expenses. Further contention of the petitioner is that, prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy, aged about 33 years, Heavy Transport Vehicle driver and getting an income of Rs.20,000/- per month. Due to the accident, he is completely bedridden, and lost his earnings.
